newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-U.S. OPEN COURSE, HOLE BY HOLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-U.S. OPEN COURSE, HOLE BY HOLE.

text.p: The U.S. Open has returned to Washington's Congressional Country Club for the first time in 33 years.
Here is a brief hole-by-hole look at the 7,213-yard, par-70 course -- the longest in Open history.

No. 1, par 4, 402 yards - With an elevated tee and a relatively wide fairway, the opening hole offers a friendly welcome to Congressional. The green is protected by three bunkers but is fairly flat, offering the best birdie chance for a while.

No. 2, par 3, 235 yards - The fun begins here. This long, uphill par 3 requires a high, soft tee shot to a bowl-shaped green with a flagstick that may not be totally visible. Six deep bunkers surround the green, which has a ridge dissecting it, creating two distinct landing areas.
No. 3, par 4, 455 yards - Trees on the left and bunkers on the right make an accurate tee shot crucial to set up a long uphill approach to a well-bunkered green.

No. 4, par 4, 434 yards - This is one of the holes significantly redesigned for the Open. A blind tee shot was removed but the target area, while visible, is still narrow and guarded by big trees. The green is no bargain either, sloping severely from back to front.

No. 5, par 4, 407 yards - This relatively short left-dogleg hole is made challenging by a sloping fairway protected by bunkers on the left and big mounds on the right. Three deep bunkers surround the green.

No. 6, par 4, 475 yards - Normally a par 5, this devillish hole may be the toughest in the Open. It requires a long, accurate tee shot because a drive in the rough offers little chance of reaching the green, which is guarded by a pond on the front and right.
No. 7, par 3, 174 yards - This par 3 features an uphill tee shot to a very dangerous green, which has two terraces with very steep slopes. Three will be a good score here.

No. 8, par 4, 362 yards - The shortest par 4 at Congresional has a sharp right dogleg, a very narrow fairway and a small green, but it is still one of the more realistic birdie opportunities, as long as one avoids the five bunkers protecting the green.
No. 9, par 5, 607 yards - One of the longest in Open history, this hole has a deep ravine in front of the green that will probably force even the longest hitters to lay up and attack with a wedge.

No. 10, par 4, 466 yards - The final nine begins with one of Congressional's toughest -- a very long, uphill hole with a tilted fairway that the members play as a par 5. A stream runs along the right side of the narrow fairway and feeds a pond bordering the right side of the subtly undulating green, which is also protected by big bunkers on the left.

No. 11, par 4, 415 yards - The sharp left dogleg with bunkers on the right will induce many players to hit irons off the tee, but they will still have relatively short downhill approaches to a green that runs from left to right.
No. 12, par 3, 187 yards - The wide green is an inviting target but it is shallow and slopes severely from back to front, offering several very difficult pin locations.

No. 13, par 4, 461 yards - With out of bounds on the left, a deep hollow on the right and unforgiving rough all round, this brute requires an accurate tee shot, but things don't get easier. The semi-blind uphill approach is to a severely sloping, two-tier green guarded by four bunkers.

No. 14, par 4, 439 yards - Four bunkers along the right fairway make it a challenging drive from an elevated tee. The well-bunkered, elevated green, which is hard to see from the fairway, has a ridge splitting it in two which should make for some very interesting putts.

No. 15, par 5, 583 yards - This par 5 may be reachable in two shots by some long hitters, but only with a heroic uphill drive. A series of bunkers guards the front of the green, especially on the right. However, the slightly elevated green is relatively flat and should yield some birdies.
No. 16, par 4, 441 yards - A severe dropoff in the fairway will prompt many players to lay up off the tee, which will leave them a long approach to yet another well-bunkered green.

No. 17, par 4, 480 yards - Congressional's signature hole is a long, slight dogleg left that runs downhill to a green nestled on the shore of a lake, with water bordering three sides. A ridge defines the left rear of the putting surface, which should offer at least one extremely difficult pin position -- probably Sunday.

No. 18, par 3, 190 yards - Not since 1909 has an Open ended on a par 3. The tee shot is all carry over water with the green sitting high on the bank of the lake, just across from the 17th green. With shaved slopes leading down to water in front and on the left, this short hole may provide more than its share of drama, especially with the championship on the line.
Who knows? Maybe a hole in one will win the Open for the first time in history.
